correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and normalization are explicit in RESULT.md. Polar scaling maps the radial hull to an icosahedron truncated at 12 vertices. For 0 <= s <= 1/2, disjoint cap pyramids yield volume vol(I)(1-3 b s^3); the polar dodecahedron gains 12 disjoint facet pyramids yielding vol(I°)/(1-bs). Its volume product is B(1-3 b s^3)/(1-bs). Exact q(s)=1-9s^2+6bs^3 has negative derivative on (0,1/2) and opposite endpoint signs; the root is unique. Exact signs at 1/3 and 9/25 and radical inequality (958-386 sqrt(5))/9375 > 0 show tau_*>1, and the final homothetic tail has constant product B. Independent numeric convex-hull/halfspace tests at seven tau values agreed within 2e-14; check.py verifies exact rational signs and prints numerical values. Numerical checks corroborate rather than prove the continuum.

originality.rationale: The closest prior result in the accessible ledger is strict Mahler-product growth only up to the unit-sphere parameter tau=1. It neither establishes validity of the branch beyond tau=1 nor its uniquely determined critical root and later decline. Hoehner 2026 and Wimmer concern ordinary volume maximization among unit-sphere-inscribed polytopes, not this affine-invariant objective or its non-spherical optimum. Other relevant work either gives universal lower bounds or unrelated polytopal families. Published-claim search did not identify implication-equivalent coverage; limitations of primary source section access are expressly recorded. This PASS reflects best-knowledge same-model historical comparison, not historical uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: The detailed Hoehner Section 7 and some plausible historical full-text treatments could not be exhaustively inspected; an older explicit equivalent formula or theorem is possible.

value.rationale: The exact natural invariant is the affine-invariant Mahler product on the canonical icosahedral/pentakis-dodecahedral orbit family motivated by the 32-vertex sphere-inscribed volume theorem. The completed post-rhombic profile has a unique optimum outside the sphere constraint, a sharp algebraic root and a nontrivial monotonicity reversal, revealing incompatibility of spherical-volume and polar-product optimization. The strictly proved tiny numerical gain is not the sole justification: the structural classification, branch endpoints, polar geometry and optimization criterion distinction are substantive.
